paragraphs.content: It is fairly obvious if youve been taking photos for long enough that it is more about your eyes over the ones you see. In the same vein, photography isn't the act of searching for a story; it is however, all to common to see people appropriate circumstances or people to tell stories that are not theirs, this pisses me off like nothing else can. This only happens because to me photography is one of the ways i get to be as vulnerable as possible, when I take shitty pictures (and believe me I take a lot) that is a reflection of a clouded state, unable to be brave, vulnerable or present. Presence here affoards me a lot in the way of memory; remembering the first time I saw a colour and the subsequent times I saw it, the memory of the emotions associated with that, presence, to see parts and wholes, and wholes of parts and their parts, what that makes me feel, and from this existence I then take photos, its is a conversation I have with myself, a conversation, the object of my photography is fairly briefly subjected to.

I feel like the way we interact with the world as people is a lot like this, where you tend to hide a lot more than you’d probably think you are, and this naturally causes problems, rifts, anger fights, but it can also just be a beautiful thing. It is kind of scary to see the direction our species seems to be heading in. The violence and scale and breadth of tragedy we are capable of is incomprehensible to me. I think people sometimes just do things because they can, and other people just seem to refuse to want to talk to them for whatever reason. I have always believed that conversation but even that seems and feels and often is just impossible. There is change and there is progress and more and more it feels like we could maybe get our shit together but in the interim to just see how things are and taking it all in it just scares me, it should scare everyone I think, maybe it doesnt because maybe people just dont know, and can you blame them?

I feel like between moments in zeitgeist theres atleast a decade long serious hangover and then the intensity decreases by half ever 5 years proceeding that, this is different for violence because that tends to stick around for however long because the effect of violence is randomly sampled over something in culture alone, which you can choose not to consume. Consumption I believe is just such a big factor for why people are so much more on edge, everything that gets created gets to everyone, theres no way to actually avoid it and that means that there is no way to perhaps slowly integrate into a society that is constantly changing, where how you interact with people is constantly changing, what it means to be in rather than out can be so hard to even understand with how much technology has changed everything and so naturally there is conflict. There is so much more room for consumption over creation, which also means there is dar less room for conversation, and observation or understanding, which I think is a tragedy in and of it self.
